facts.label: Financial base view
facts.text: PENN's reported base improved through 2026 on every measure the sources support. The company's own debt measure, traditional debt of principal outstanding, fell from 2904.1 at FY2025 to 2806.6 at 2026-09-30 while cash rose from 686.6 to 1044.8. Over the same period LTM Consolidated Adjusted EBITDA, the company's non-GAAP measure struck after triple net operating lease rent, rose from 830.1 to 1088.2, so the debt ratios on that basis fell to 2.58x gross and 1.62x net from 3.50x and 2.67x. Liquidity at 2026-09-30 is 2020.9 and no committed facility expiring within twelve months was located (the revolver matures in April 2031). Cash interest cover on LTM Consolidated Adjusted EBITDA is 2.85x. The refinancing in 2026 pushed bank maturities to 2031 and 2033, replaced the 2027 revolver and term loan maturities, and added 600.0 of 6.75% notes due 2031. The base view is limited in three ways. First, 8157.6 of lease and financing obligations to landlords sit outside the debt figure, and 4359.4 of that (financing obligations of 2309.8 and finance lease liabilities of 2049.6) is also outside the rent deduction in EBITDA, so debt ratios on the company's definition understate fixed-charge leverage; on a perimeter that adds those two items, net leverage is 5.63x. Second, the covenant tests (total net leverage 4.50x maximum and interest coverage 2.00x minimum) are described but their reported values and definitions are not supplied, so headroom is Not calculable. Third, the improvement in EBITDA depends on the Interactive segment, whose loss narrowed to 18.3 in Q3 2026 but which remains negative, and the Q3 2025 comparison is flattered by the absence of ESPN-related advertising of 52.0 (37.5 under the Sportsbook Agreement and 14.5 under the Investment Agreement, 10-Q Q3 page:41) that was in Q3 2025 media and advertising expense; the 825.0 Q3 2025 impairment distorts net income but not Consolidated Adjusted EBITDA, which adds impairment back.

facts.label: Latest quarter, financing events and after the quarter
facts.text: 2026 financing events in order. On March 16, 2026 PENN issued 600.0 of 6.75% senior unsecured notes at par, due April 1, 2031, and used the net proceeds to repay revolver borrowings (10-Q Q3 page:18). On April 16, 2026 the Third Amendment refinanced and extended the 1.0 billion revolver and the 446.9 Term Loan A to April 2031 and removed the credit spread adjustment (page:17). On May 28, 2026 the Fourth Amendment extended the 962.5 Term Loan B to May 2033 and cut margins by 50 basis points to 2.00% (page:18). The 106.7 convertible notes were repaid in May 2026 (page:19). In connection with the two amendments the Company recorded 16.3 of issuance costs and a 2.4 original issue discount (page:18). The loss on early extinguishment of debt was 1.8 for 9M 2026 and nil in Q3 2026 (10-Q Q3 page:3). On June 24, 2026 the Aurora facility opened, GLPI funded 216.3 and annual rent rose by 17.4 (10-Q Q3 pages 23 and 70). Quarter ended 2026-09-30: Q3 events are the Boomtown New Orleans relocation announced August 17, 2026 and the Council Bluffs groundbreaking on September 14, 2026 (page:48).

facts.label: Latest quarter, financing events and after the quarter
facts.text: Interactive revenue quality. Interactive revenue of 348.4 includes a gaming tax reimbursement gross-up from third-party partners of 191.4 in Q3 2026 and 139.5 in Q3 2025 (10-Q Q3 page:15). Excluding the gross-up, Interactive revenue was 157.0 in Q3 2026 against 158.2 in Q3 2025, a decline of 1.2, and for 9M 2026 493.3 against 498.3, a decline of 5.0. Interactive gaming revenue was 126.6 against 129.3 in Q3. The reported 17.0% increase in Interactive revenue (348.4 against 297.7, an increase of 50.7) is therefore more than accounted for by the gross-up, which rose by 51.9 (191.4 less 139.5). The earnings improvement came from lower costs: media and advertising fell to 39.8 from 73.0 (10-Q Q3 pages 38 and 40), and Q3 2025 media and advertising included 52.0 of ESPN-related advertising (10-Q Q3 page:41); the Sportsbook Agreement was terminated on November 5, 2025 (page:12).

facts.label: Business and transaction view
facts.text: PENN is a public company without a sponsor or controlling holder disclosed in the supplied text. It runs regional casinos and racetracks and an online sports betting and iCasino business across North America, and its real estate sits mostly with landlords under long-dated triple net leases. For a creditor the structure matters more than the brand: the retail segments produce the cash flow, rent is a fixed and escalating operating cost paid before debt service and a lease default is also a debt default, and the Interactive segment is moving toward break-even by cutting cost rather than by growing underlying revenue. The 2026 transactions were refinancings and development financings rather than a change of control: a new 600.0 unsecured note, extended bank maturities, and sale-leaseback funding from GLPI for the Aurora project. The history that matters is the 2023 Barstool round trip, the 2023 to 2025 ESPN relationship and its early end, the 2025 to 2026 activist contest settled by a cooperation agreement, and the shift from buybacks in 2025 to none in 2026. Creditor protections in the credit agreement and indentures, board composition detail and large-holder data are not supplied, so legal capacity to pay out cash, incur debt or release collateral is not assessed and the governance read relies on documented actions only.

facts.label: Transaction summary and new debt issues
facts.text: There is no change-of-control, acquisition or sponsor transaction in the period, and no transaction source for one; the transaction rows below are financing and development events. On March 16, 2026 PENN issued 600.0 of 6.75% senior unsecured notes at par due April 1, 2031, callable from April 1, 2028 at declining premiums, interest payable each April 1 and October 1; the notes are not guaranteed by subsidiaries unless certain subsidiary-guaranteed debt securities are later issued, and net proceeds repaid revolver borrowings (10-Q Q3 page:18). Issuance costs were 10.3. On April 16, 2026 the Third Amendment refinanced and extended the 1.0 billion revolver and the 446.9 Term Loan A to April 2031, removed the credit spread adjustment, with margins of 1.50% to 2.25% over Term SOFR (10-Q Q3 page:17). On May 28, 2026 the Fourth Amendment extended the 962.5 Term Loan B to May 2033 and cut margins by 50 basis points to 2.00% over Term SOFR, with a SOFR floor of 0.50% (page:18); issuance costs of 16.3 and an original issue discount of 2.4 were recorded for the two amendments. In May 2026 the remaining 106.7 of the 2.75% convertible notes was repaid at maturity. The result at 2026-09-30 is total debt principal of 2806.6 (CP-1), with the nearest large maturity the 400.0 5.625% Notes due January 15, 2027 which are classified long-term on the Company's "intent and ability to refinance on a long-term basis" (page:19).

facts.label: Credit translations
facts.text: 1. Landlord claims and cross-default. Evidence: the AR PENN and 2023 Master Leases are "cross-defaulted, cross-collateralized, and coterminous, and subject to a parent guarantee" (10-Q Q3 page:21), and a default under a master lease "could result in a default under our debt agreements" (10-K page:35). Risk mechanic: a lease default or termination removes operating properties and accelerates debt through cross-default, so lease performance gates the whole capital structure. Credit implication: lease coverage and rent escalation are first-order credit drivers alongside debt leverage; GLPI funding of development raises fixed rent (analyst arithmetic: 10.1, 11.7 and 17.4 of added annual rent on 130.0, 150.0 and 216.3 of funding, or 7.9% on 496.3 in total). Category: Analyst Interpretation on Documentary Facts. 2. Refinancing and maturity. Evidence: bank facilities now mature in 2031 and 2033 and 600.0 of notes was issued due 2031 (10-Q Q3 pages 17-18). facts.label: Credit view
facts.text: PENN's fundamental credit profile is improving but still burdened by landlord obligations, so the view is constructive on liquidity and refinancing and cautious on fixed charges. The strongest support is liquidity of USD 2,020.9 million and net debt of 1.62x LTM Consolidated Adjusted EBITDA of USD 1,088.2 million, with bank maturities pushed to 2031 and 2033. The weakest point is that USD 8,157.6 million of lease and financing obligations sit outside debt and cross-default into the debt agreements, and that the online segment still loses money. What decides the outcome is whether the retail margin gains and online cost savings hold while rent escalates, and whether the USD 400.0 million of notes due January 15, 2027 are refinanced on acceptable terms. [CP-1; CP-1A]

facts.label: Key findings
facts.text: PENN's reported leverage fell through 2026 on the company's own definition. Total debt over LTM Consolidated Adjusted EBITDA is 2.58x against 3.50x at FY2025, and net debt over EBITDA is 1.62x against 2.67x, as cash rose to USD 1,044.8 million and EBITDA rose to USD 1,088.2 million from USD 830.1 million [CP-1 Chart data: leverage]. The measure is management's non-GAAP view struck after triple net operating lease rent and it leaves out USD 4,359.4 million of financing obligations and finance leases, so an extended perimeter that adds them gives net leverage of 5.63x [CP-1 Calculations]. Creditors should therefore treat the improvement as real but read the level against the landlord claims, not against the headline ratio.

facts.label: Key findings
facts.text: Liquidity is the clearest strength. Cash of USD 1,044.8 million plus an undrawn revolver of USD 976.1 million gives USD 2,020.9 million, against USD 432.3 million of debt maturing in the next twelve months and no committed facility located that expires within that period [CP-1 Chart data: liquidity; CP-1 Calculations]. The 2026 refinancing extended the revolver and Term Loan A to April 2031 and Term Loan B to May 2033 and added USD 600.0 million of 6.75% notes due 2031 [CP-1A Transaction summary and new debt issues]. The near-term maturity that remains is the USD 400.0 million of 5.625% notes due January 15, 2027, which the company classifies as long-term on its intent and ability to refinance.

facts.label: Key findings
facts.text: The earnings recovery has two unequal sources. Retail Segment Adjusted EBITDAR was USD 501.8 million in Q3 2026 against USD 465.8 million, with the margin at 33.7% against 32.8% [CP-1 Financials and credit metrics]. The online segment's loss narrowed to USD 18.3 million from USD 76.6 million, but revenue excluding the gaming tax gross-up was USD 157.0 million against USD 158.2 million, and online gaming revenue fell, so the gain came from lower marketing, general and administrative and labor costs after the ESPN agreement ended [CP-1; CP-1A Company and operating model]. That makes part of the earnings recovery depend on keeping costs low.

facts.label: Key findings
facts.text: Fixed charges remain heavy. LTM cash paid for interest of USD 382.4 million gives cash interest cover of 2.85x on LTM Consolidated Adjusted EBITDA, up from 2.17x at FY2025 [CP-1 Chart data: interest cover]. Leases are the structural issue: the AR PENN and 2023 Master Leases are cross-defaulted and a master lease default could trigger a default under the debt agreements, and the development funding GLPI provides adds annual rent of about 7.9% of the funds received [CP-1A Credit translations]. Covenant headroom is not measurable: the maximum total net leverage of 4.50x and minimum interest coverage of 2.00x are printed but the reported ratios and definitions are not supplied [CP-1 Covenants].

facts.label: Strengths and weaknesses
facts.text: Strengths. Liquidity and refinancing runway [Documentary Fact]: PENN holds cash of USD 1,044.8 million and an undrawn revolver of USD 976.1 million maturing April 2031, so liquidity of USD 2,020.9 million covers the USD 432.3 million of twelve-month maturities several times over, and bank maturities now sit in 2031 and 2033 [CP-1 Chart data: liquidity; CP-1A Transaction summary and new debt issues]. Deleveraging on management measures [Documentary Fact for the figures, Analyst Interpretation for the reading]: total debt fell to USD 2,806.6 million from USD 2,904.1 million while LTM Consolidated Adjusted EBITDA rose to USD 1,088.2 million, giving 2.58x gross and 1.62x net, which lowers the burden of the floating term loans and eases refinancing [CP-1 Chart data: leverage]. Retail earnings power [Documentary Fact]: Segment Adjusted EBITDAR of USD 501.8 million in Q3 2026 on a 33.7% margin, spread across 28 jurisdictions and 42 gaming and racing properties, supports cash flow from a diversified base [CP-1 Financials and credit metrics; CP-1A Company and operating model]. Governance record [Analyst Interpretation]: no priming, uptier, drop-down or collateral release was found, buybacks of USD 354.4 million in FY2025 stopped in nine months 2026, and the February 2026 activist settlement removed an open contest, which is supportive of creditors though the debt documents that would constrain future behaviour are not supplied [CP-1A Ownership, governance and capital allocation].

facts.label: Strengths and weaknesses
facts.text: Weaknesses. Landlord obligations [Documentary Fact for amounts, Analyst Interpretation for the reading]: lease and financing obligations of USD 8,157.6 million sit outside the debt figure, of which USD 4,359.4 million is not deducted in EBITDA, so fixed-charge leverage is far higher than the headline, and a lease default is also a debt default [CP-1 Claims outside debt; CP-1A Credit translations]. Online segment [Analyst Interpretation]: a loss of USD 18.3 million in Q3 2026 and a loss of USD 78.6 million over the LTM period mean the segment still consumes cash, and the improvement rests on cost cuts with revenue ex gross-up flat, so earnings could slip if marketing returns [CP-1A Company and operating model]. Interest burden [Documentary Fact]: cash interest of USD 382.4 million against LTM Consolidated Adjusted EBITDA of USD 1,088.2 million leaves cover of 2.85x, and LTM net income was a loss of USD 11.0 million [CP-1 Financials and credit metrics]. Earnings quality [Documentary Fact]: Consolidated Adjusted EBITDA is a management measure that adds back items including USD 44.9 million labelled Other for nine months 2026, so its underlying level cannot be tested against the ledger [CP-1 Quality and definition notes on EBITDA]. Information gaps [Insufficient Information]: covenant ratios, guarantor identity, restricted-payment capacity, large-holder data and ratings are not supplied, which prevents a view on headroom and creditor protections and limits confidence to Medium [CP-0; CP-1A Gaps].

facts.label: Evidence trace view
facts.text: Every material claim in the four handoffs was traced to a located source span, and the arithmetic was recomputed from the cited figures. The headline financial claims hold: debt principal of 2,806.6 and cash of 1,044.8 at 2026-09-30, liquidity of 2,020.9, LTM Consolidated Adjusted EBITDA of 1,088.2, and the ratios derived from them, all recompute exactly and share one perimeter and period basis. A set of 186 figure and phrase checks against the cited pages found 179 at the cited location; the other 7 were examined individually and two were real locator errors, the rest check-string artifacts or an adjacent page already cited. The audit found six issues, all minor: wrong page numbers for three cash-flow lines and one working-capital reference, a statement that gaming taxes are the largest retail cost that is true for only two of four retail segments, a landlord-payment figure of 252.2 that should read 263.3, a gap for the 4.125% notes that the 10-K fills, and a cross-default described more broadly than the filing supports in two handoffs. None changes a ratio, a liquidity figure or the direction of the credit view, so the run is graded Passed with corrections logged. The strongest contrary reading is that the improvement is overstated: the company's debt measure leaves out financing obligations and finance leases of 4,359.4 and LTM net income is a loss of 11.0, so the handoffs already carry the extended-perimeter leverage of 5.63x. What would make the contrary view win is covenant definitions that count those obligations as debt, which the missing credit agreement prevents anyone from testing.

spans.text: ## Request

Issuer: PENN Entertainment, Inc. (ticker PENN, Pennsylvania corporation, Commission file number 0-24206). As-of date and cutoff: 2026-11-05. Pathway: credit_snapshot. Reporting currency: USD; figures are in USD millions unless stated. Current period q3-2026 (quarter and nine months ended 2026-09-30); prior period fy-2025 (year ended 2025-12-31). Requested downstream modules: CP-1, CP-1A, CP-2, CP-5.

Question this handoff answers: can the supplied source set support the requested work, and what remains blocked? It gives no credit conclusion, legal interpretation or investment opinion. Source sufficiency is kept separate from completion of downstream analysis. The context file (sha256 de76f6d737b4f874d55cfe4efb68426523509ccefb05817de5c048370ec1b054) holds run settings, not issuer evidence. It leaves ratings, quotes, deal terms, valuation inputs, assumptions and research questions blank. Those blanks are not zero and are carried as gaps.
## Sources
### Issuer sources relied on

All seven are text extractions (JSONL, one record per `page:N` chunk). The sha256 is that of the supplied extraction file. Each extraction also prints its own inner "Visible text of ..." hash on `page:1`; the two differ and the file hash is the identifier used here.

### Supplied handoffs
None. CP-0 is the first module; the run supplies no upstream handoff to it (`handoffs` is empty in the request).
### Not in the pack and not used
`_retrieval.json` is ignored by the run and is not evidence. No outside knowledge of the company is used.
## Findings
### Reader summary
| Bottom line | Confidence | Main limitation |

| The seven supplied PENN filings and releases support financial extraction, business and transaction context, and later synthesis and review, with bounded limits. Debt, liquidity, segments and covenants are printed with locators. | Medium | Executed credit agreement, indentures and master leases are not supplied, so covenant definitions and headroom cannot be tested; text extraction only. |
| Finding | Creditor impact | Confidence |

| Debt by instrument, maturities, letters of credit and revolver availability are printed in the latest quarterly filing. | Facility-level debt and liquidity can be extracted from a filed source. | High |

| Covenant levels are printed but the reported covenant ratios are not; only a compliance statement is given. | Headroom to the leverage and coverage tests cannot be measured from these sources. | High |

| Lease obligations to the real estate landlords are large and are described in filings, but the executed lease documents are not supplied. | Lease terms, cross-default and cure mechanics rest on filing summaries only. | Medium |

| Earnings releases state management measures that differ in definition from the filed statements and from the covenant ratios. | Management leverage figures cannot stand in for covenant tests. | Medium |
### Readiness view

The effective source set is READY_WITH_LIMITATIONS for the requested credit snapshot. The three quarterly filings and the audited annual report are filed statements for the same consolidated issuer, PENN Entertainment, Inc., and carry period labels, a debt note, a lease note, a segment note, supplemental cash-flow disclosure and a liquidity discussion. The releases add reconciliations and management narrative and are treated as attributed supporting claims. They never override a filing. No source is blocked, no identity boundary is unresolved, and no critical document is absent for a filing-based snapshot. The limits below are bounded and are carried to each consumer. Source sufficiency is asserted only (SOURCE_SUFFICIENCY_ONLY). No normalized quarters, reconciliation or downstream input acceptance is asserted here.
### Source-by-source assessment
| Source | Evidence located | Limitation carried forward |

| 10-K FY2025 | Cover: "For the fiscal year ended December 31, 2025" (page:1). Item 8 (page:100), auditor opinion (page:101), critical audit matter on the Interactive reporting unit goodwill test (page:103). Debt note 10 with year-end 2025 table and repayment schedule (page:137). Covenants and compliance statement (page:90). Cash paid for interest in the cash-flow supplement (page:109). Exhibit index listing legal documents by reference (page:197). | Executed agreements are listed in the index, not supplied. |

| 10-Q Q1 2026 | Cover "quarterly period ended March 31, 2026" (page:1). Balance sheet with cash (page:2). Revolver availability and letters of credit (page:16). 6.75% notes issuance (page:16). | Unaudited; superseded for point-in-time balances by later quarters but needed for the quarter series. |

| 10-Q Q2 2026 | Cover "quarterly period ended June 30, 2026" (page:1). Balance sheet with cash (page:2). Third Amendment Agreement (page:18). Covenant compliance statement (page:21). | Unaudited. Six-month and quarter columns must stay separate. |

| 10-Q Q3 2026 | Balance sheet, operations, cash flows (pages 2-6). Note 4 revenue by segment (page:15). Note 5 debt table and repayment schedule (pages 15-16). Credit facility terms, covenants, letters of credit (pages 17-18). Note 6 leases (pages 20-22). Note 13 segments with Segment Adjusted EBITDAR and reconciliation to net income (pages 37-40). MD&A liquidity and cash flow (pages 69-70). | Unaudited; nine-month cash flow is year to date, with no discrete third-quarter cash-flow statement in the filing. |
| Release Q1 2026 | Retail highlights, total liquidity and traditional net debt, leverage table (pages 1-6). | Management measures, non-GAAP. Dated 2026-04-23. |
| Release Q2 2026 | Total liquidity, traditional net debt, leverage table (pages 3-8). | Management measures, non-GAAP. Dated 2026-08-06. |

| Release Q3 2026 | Segment table, reconciliation of net income to Consolidated Adjusted EBITDA, selected financial information and ratios, cash flow data, non-GAAP definitions (pages 3-12). | Management measures, non-GAAP. Dated the cutoff day, so it is the last permitted evidence date. |
### Entity, perimeter and instrument roles

The issuer and filer is PENN Entertainment, Inc.; the statements are consolidated ("PENN Entertainment, Inc. and its subsidiaries", 10-Q Q3 page:7). The senior notes are issued by the Company. The 10-Q Q3 states the 6.75% Notes are "not guaranteed by any of the Company’s subsidiaries except in the event that the Company, in the future, issues certain subsidiary-guaranteed debt securities" (page:18); the same wording is given for the 5.625% Notes. The 10-K states that gaming and related assets "collateralize our obligations under our Amended Credit Facilities" (page:64), and the index lists "guarantors party thereto" for the credit agreement (10-K page:197). The identity of those guarantors and the restricted perimeter is therefore not located in the supplied text and is carried as a gap. The real estate landlords are Gaming and Leisure Properties, Inc. (GLPI) and VICI Properties Inc. (VICI), who are counterparties and not issuers or guarantors. The AR PENN Master Lease and the 2023 Master Lease are "cross-defaulted, cross-collateralized, and coterminous, and subject to a parent guarantee" (10-Q Q3 page:21). No parent, sponsor or borrower distinct from the issuer is named in the context or sources.
### Version relationships and conflicts

The three quarterly filings and the annual report are sequential periods of the same issuer, not duplicates; each stays an active source. The facility structure changed during the run period: the Third Amendment of 2026-04-16 refinanced the revolver and Term Loan A to April 2031, and the Fourth Amendment of 2026-05-28 extended the Term Loan B to May 2033 (10-Q Q3 pages 17-18). The year-end 2025 debt table (revolver due 2027, Term Loan A due 2027, Term Loan B due 2029; 10-K page:137) therefore describes an earlier facility version and cannot be mixed with the 2026-09-30 table without labelling.

No conflict between a release and a filing was found in the items checked. Two figures that look alike are different measures. Cash paid for interest is 291.6 for the nine months in the cash-flow statement ("Cash paid for interest, net of amounts capitalized", 10-Q Q3 page:6). The release gives 100.9 for the same nine months as "Cash paid for interest on traditional debt" (release Q3 page:8). The release describes the narrower measure. A downstream user must not treat the two as the same quantity. Likewise the Q3 segment total of Segment Adjusted EBITDAR (483.5, 10-Q Q3 page:38) differs from the retail-only figure of 501.8 in the release (page:1) because the Interactive loss of 18.3 is netted in the first.
### Consumer assessments
| Consumer | Status | Evidence demand and basis | Limitations carried |

| CP-1 financial data extraction | READY_WITH_LIMITATIONS | Statements, discrete and year-to-date periods, facility-level debt with carrying and principal amounts, segment revenue and Segment Adjusted EBITDAR, add-backs in the release reconciliation, cash paid for interest and taxes, and lease balances are all located in the filings. | Covenant ratio values are not printed. A discrete third-quarter cash-flow statement is not in the filing. Lease cash rent comes from release or MD&A text only. Management measures are not covenant measures. |

| CP-1A business and transaction context | READY_WITH_LIMITATIONS | Business description and segment grid (10-Q Q3 pages 7-8, 10-K pages 6 onward), master lease structure, the 2026 refinancing events, the ESPN Sportsbook Agreement termination (10-Q Q3 page:12), the HG Vora cooperation agreement costs (10-Q Q3 pages 44 and 58), and post-period items are in the filings. No dedicated subsequent-events note was located in the Q3 10-Q on search. | Executed lease, credit and indenture documents are not supplied. Ownership detail beyond share counts is not supplied. |

| CP-5 evidence trace review | READY_WITH_LIMITATIONS | Cited quotes can be matched to the retained page chunks of seven sources. | Review of a locator is a check against extracted text, not against the rendered filing. Charts and images are not covered. |
## Calculations

No analytical metric is derived in this module. The checks below only tie printed totals to their printed components, to show the extraction is internally consistent. Units are USD millions. They are not a credit calculation and do not normalize or reconcile any figure.
| Check | Inputs (locator) | Result |
| Repayment schedule at 2026-09-30 | 8.1 + 433.1 + 33.1 + 433.2 + 33.2 + 1,865.9 (10-Q Q3 page:16) | 2,806.6, equal to the printed total minimum payments |

| Revolver availability at 2026-09-30 | 1,000.0 revolver less 23.9 letters of credit (10-Q Q3 pages 17-18; the 1.0 billion size is stated as "$1.0 billion Amended Revolving Credit Facility") | 976.1, equal to the printed "$976.1 million" |
| Three-month revenue by segment, Q3 2026 | 708.3 + 291.8 + 147.5 + 341.9 + 348.4 + 4.0 - 1.9 (10-Q Q3 page:15) | 1,840.0, equal to printed total revenues |

| Segment Adjusted EBITDAR to Consolidated Adjusted EBITDA, Q3 2026 | 208.1 + 108.3 + 50.9 + 134.5 - 18.3 = 483.5; less other category 31.6; less rent expense on triple net operating leases 167.9 (10-Q Q3 page:38; release Q3 pages 3-4) | 284.0, equal to the printed Consolidated Adjusted EBITDA |
| Nine-month version of the same bridge | 622.8 + 321.5 + 159.9 + 386.2 - 38.7 - 94.9 - 494.4 (release Q3 pages 3-4) | 862.4, equal to the printed total |
| Traditional net debt, 2026-09-30 | 2,806.6 less cash 1,044.8 (release Q3 page:7) | 1,761.8, equal to the printed figure |

| Total liquidity as the release describes it | cash 1,044.8 plus revolver availability 976.1 (10-Q Q3 pages 2 and 18) | 2,020.9, consistent with the release statement "Total liquidity as of September 30, 2026 was $2.0 billion" (page:2) |

Release ratios checked against their stated definitions (release Q3 pages 7, 11, 12). Lease-adjusted net leverage: (7,940.0 + 1,761.8) / (1,088.2 + 656.2) = 9,701.8 / 1,744.4, which rounds to 5.6x, the printed figure. Traditional net leverage: 1,761.8 / (1,088.2 + 656.2 - 992.5) = 1,761.8 / 751.9, which rounds to 2.3x, the printed figure, where 992.5 is 7,940.0 divided by 8, the trailing cash rent to REIT landlords. These ties confirm the extraction only. They are management definitions and are not the covenant ratio in the Second Amended and Restated Credit Agreement.

Not calculable in this module: covenant total net leverage and interest coverage, because the covenant definitions are in the credit agreement, which is not supplied, and no reported covenant ratio value was found.
## Gaps

Guidance is Not supplied. | Low | CP-1A, CP-2 | Obtain the guidance slides or the earlier outlook release. |

No document is dated after the 2026-11-05 cutoff. The latest evidence is the release and the Q3 10-Q, both on the cutoff date. Events after 2026-09-30 in the Q3 10-Q (for example the 2026-10-15 notice to redeem exchangeable shares on or about 2026-12-15, page:31) are subsequent events and are labelled as such. A future date such as the 2027 maturity of the 5.625% Notes is a contract term, not a fact after the cutoff.
## Next module

Proceed to CP-1 (financial data) on the 10-Q Q3 filing and the 10-K as primary sources, with the releases as supporting claims. Carry forward: the facility version change, the distinction between management and covenant measures, the cash-paid-for-interest definition difference, the absence of covenant ratio values and guarantor detail, and year-to-date versus discrete period labels. CP-1A, CP-2 and CP-5 follow in the run order. Next evidence action for the owner: obtain the credit agreement with compliance certificate, the indentures and the executed master leases.

spans.text: ## Request

Issuer: PENN Entertainment, Inc. (Nasdaq: PENN), consolidated. As-of date and cutoff: 2026-11-05. Pathway: credit_snapshot. Reporting currency USD, in millions unless stated. Current period q3-2026 (three and nine months ended 2026-09-30); prior period fy-2025 (year ended 2025-12-31). Task: extract and organise the financial base for a creditor view: reported statements, debt by instrument, liquidity, maturities, leases and other claims outside debt, covenants, the latest quarter and events to the cutoff. Every derived figure is shown in `## Calculations`. Period labels used throughout: Q3 2026 (three months), 9M 2026 (nine months), LTM Q3 2026 (twelve months to 2026-09-30), FY2025, and the same for prior-year comparatives.

Perimeter: PENN Entertainment, Inc. and subsidiaries, as consolidated in the filings. The filings contain no separate issuer-level or subsidiary statements. The perimeter is the same for every figure below.
## Sources
### Issuer sources relied on
| Source name | sha256 |

Authority: the filings (10-K audited, 10-Qs unaudited) control reported facts. The releases are management documents and are used for the non-GAAP Consolidated Adjusted EBITDA, the lease-adjusted measures and discrete-quarter items, always labelled as management measures. The context file (sha256 de76f6d737b4f874d55cfe4efb68426523509ccefb05817de5c048370ec1b054) is run settings, not evidence.

Locators are written `source page:N`, where N is the chunk number in the supplied extraction, not the printed page. "10-Q Q3" means the 10-Q for the quarter ended 2026-09-30; "release Q3" means the exhibit dated 2026-11-05.
### Supplied handoffs
| Module | sha256 |
| CP-0 | 8e6b52c72fe186ee073cb0e5f0c242ec3f53d4e3a091c87a50ef71a77d1acea5 |

How CP-0 is used and one correction. CP-0 rated the pack READY_WITH_LIMITATIONS and carried: no executed credit agreement, indentures or leases; no reported covenant ratio values; management measures differ from covenant and GAAP measures; the debt table changed version in 2026; and cash paid for interest has two definitions. This handoff keeps all of them. One correction: CP-0 wrote that lease cash rent comes from release or MD&A text only. It is also in the filed 10-Q Q3 Note 6, "Total payments made under our Triple Net Leases" (10-Q Q3 page:27: 251.8 for Q3 2026 and 746.6 for 9M 2026), so the filing supports it.
## Findings
### Reader summary
| Bottom line | Confidence | Main limitation |

| Financial leverage on the company's debt definition fell to 2.58x gross and 1.62x net at LTM Q3 2026, with liquidity of 2020.9, but lease and financing obligations of 8157.6 sit outside that debt. | Medium | Covenant ratios and definitions are not supplied, so covenant headroom cannot be measured. |
| Finding | Creditor impact | Confidence |

| Debt principal of 2806.6 is mostly term loans due 2031 to 2033 and notes; 400.0 of notes mature in January 2027, within twelve months. | Near-term maturity is covered by cash of 1044.8 and an undrawn revolver. | High |

| LTM Consolidated Adjusted EBITDA rose to 1088.2 from 830.1 at FY2025, mainly from a smaller Interactive loss and higher Retail earnings. | Stronger earnings drive the lower leverage; Interactive still loses money. | Medium |

| Financing obligations of 2309.8 and finance lease liabilities of 2049.6 are outside debt and outside the EBITDA deduction; adding them lifts net leverage to 5.63x. | Debt-like landlord claims are the larger part of fixed obligations. | Medium |

| Cash paid for interest was 382.4 over the last twelve months, giving 2.85x cover from LTM Consolidated Adjusted EBITDA. | Cover has improved but remains modest against fixed lease and interest costs. | Medium |
### Financial base view

PENN's reported base improved through 2026 on every measure the sources support. The company's own debt measure, traditional debt of principal outstanding, fell from 2904.1 at FY2025 to 2806.6 at 2026-09-30 while cash rose from 686.6 to 1044.8. Over the same period LTM Consolidated Adjusted EBITDA, the company's non-GAAP measure struck after triple net operating lease rent, rose from 830.1 to 1088.2, so the debt ratios on that basis fell to 2.58x gross and 1.62x net from 3.50x and 2.67x. Liquidity at 2026-09-30 is 2020.9 and no committed facility expiring within twelve months was located (the revolver matures in April 2031). Cash interest cover on LTM Consolidated Adjusted EBITDA is 2.85x. The refinancing in 2026 pushed bank maturities to 2031 and 2033, replaced the 2027 revolver and term loan maturities, and added 600.0 of 6.75% notes due 2031. The base view is limited in three ways. First, 8157.6 of lease and financing obligations to landlords sit outside the debt figure, and 4359.4 of that (financing obligations of 2309.8 and finance lease liabilities of 2049.6) is also outside the rent deduction in EBITDA, so debt ratios on the company's definition understate fixed-charge leverage; on a perimeter that adds those two items, net leverage is 5.63x. Second, the covenant tests (total net leverage 4.50x maximum and interest coverage 2.00x minimum) are described but their reported values and definitions are not supplied, so headroom is Not calculable. Third, the improvement in EBITDA depends on the Interactive segment, whose loss narrowed to 18.3 in Q3 2026 but which remains negative, and the Q3 2025 comparison is flattered by the absence of ESPN-related advertising of 52.0 (37.5 under the Sportsbook Agreement and 14.5 under the Investment Agreement, 10-Q Q3 page:41) that was in Q3 2025 media and advertising expense; the 825.0 Q3 2025 impairment distorts net income but not Consolidated Adjusted EBITDA, which adds impairment back.
### Chart data: leverage

### Latest quarter, financing events and after the quarter

2026 financing events in order. On March 16, 2026 PENN issued 600.0 of 6.75% senior unsecured notes at par, due April 1, 2031, and used the net proceeds to repay revolver borrowings (10-Q Q3 page:18). On April 16, 2026 the Third Amendment refinanced and extended the 1.0 billion revolver and the 446.9 Term Loan A to April 2031 and removed the credit spread adjustment (page:17). On May 28, 2026 the Fourth Amendment extended the 962.5 Term Loan B to May 2033 and cut margins by 50 basis points to 2.00% (page:18). The 106.7 convertible notes were repaid in May 2026 (page:19). In connection with the two amendments the Company recorded 16.3 of issuance costs and a 2.4 original issue discount (page:18). The loss on early extinguishment of debt was 1.8 for 9M 2026 and nil in Q3 2026 (10-Q Q3 page:3). On June 24, 2026 the Aurora facility opened, GLPI funded 216.3 and annual rent rose by 17.4 (10-Q Q3 pages 23 and 70). Quarter ended 2026-09-30: Q3 events are the Boomtown New Orleans relocation announced August 17, 2026 and the Council Bluffs groundbreaking on September 14, 2026 (page:48).

Events after 2026-09-30 and up to the cutoff, labelled subsequent: on October 15, 2026 the Company gave notice that it will redeem all outstanding exchangeable shares for common stock on or about December 15, 2026 (98,920 shares outstanding at 2026-09-30; 10-Q Q3 page:31); effective November 1, 2026 the fixed rent under the AR PENN Master Lease rose by 4.4 (page:21); the shares outstanding at October 29, 2026 were 134,253,794 (page:1). No debt event after 2026-09-30 was located. No dedicated subsequent-events note was found.

Q3 2026 against Q3 2025, from the statements and segment note. Revenue 1840.0 against 1717.3, an increase of 7.1%. Consolidated Adjusted EBITDA 284.0 against 194.9, an increase of 89.1. By component of that increase: Interactive improved by 58.3 (a loss of 18.3 against 76.6), the four retail segments by 36.0 (501.8 against 465.8), the Other category by 4.6, and triple net operating lease rent rose by 9.8, which reduces EBITDA. The retail margin was 33.7% (501.8 over 1489.5) against 32.8% (465.8 over 1418.1). Management states in the release that the "healthy operating trends" continued through October (release Q3 page:1); this is a management claim, not tested here.

Interactive revenue quality. Interactive revenue of 348.4 includes a gaming tax reimbursement gross-up from third-party partners of 191.4 in Q3 2026 and 139.5 in Q3 2025 (10-Q Q3 page:15). Excluding the gross-up, Interactive revenue was 157.0 in Q3 2026 against 158.2 in Q3 2025, a decline of 1.2, and for 9M 2026 493.3 against 498.3, a decline of 5.0. Interactive gaming revenue was 126.6 against 129.3 in Q3. The reported 17.0% increase in Interactive revenue (348.4 against 297.7, an increase of 50.7) is therefore more than accounted for by the gross-up, which rose by 51.9 (191.4 less 139.5). The earnings improvement came from lower costs: media and advertising fell to 39.8 from 73.0 (10-Q Q3 pages 38 and 40), and Q3 2025 media and advertising included 52.0 of ESPN-related advertising (10-Q Q3 page:41); the Sportsbook Agreement was terminated on November 5, 2025 (page:12).

### Covenants

The Amended Credit Facilities contain a maximum total net leverage ratio of 4.50 to 1.00, with a step up to 5.00 to 1.00 for certain significant acquisitions, and a minimum interest coverage ratio of 2.00 to 1.00, each "as defined within the Second Amended and Restated Credit Agreement" (10-Q Q3 page:17). The Company states it "was in compliance with all required financial covenants" at 2026-09-30 and expects to remain so for at least twelve months (page:20); the same statement is made at 2026-03-31, 2026-06-30 and 2025-12-31. No step-down is printed. The reported covenant ratio values are Not supplied. Headroom is Not calculable because the agreement is not supplied and the definitions may treat leases, add-backs and cash differently. The metrics computed above differ from the covenant: they are the company's non-GAAP Consolidated Adjusted EBITDA on a principal-debt basis, with cash interest that includes lease interest. The notes and credit agreement also carry cross-default provisions tied to the Master Leases (page:20). The Master Leases (AR PENN and 2023) are cross-defaulted, cross-collateralized and coterminous, with a parent guarantee (page:21).
### Quality and definition notes on EBITDA

Consolidated Adjusted EBITDA adds back stock-based compensation (47.2 for 9M 2026), pre-opening expenses (29.0), impairment, and "Other" of 44.9 for 9M 2026, described as transaction costs, restructuring (severance) and settlement costs and legal and advisory fees for the HG Vora Cooperation Agreement (release Q3 pages 6-7). It is struck after triple net operating lease rent but before interest and depreciation on finance leases and financing obligations; 9M 2026 cash paid to REIT landlords of 746.6 exceeds operating lease rent expense of 494.4 by 252.2, which is the part of landlord payments not deducted in EBITDA. Cash paid for interest on traditional debt only was 100.9 for 9M 2026 against 291.6 cash paid for interest in the cash-flow statement; the cash-flow figure includes lease and financing obligation interest (interest on finance leases 80.8 and on financing obligations 108.8 for 9M 2026, 10-Q Q3 page:28). The sum of 100.9, 80.8 and 108.8 is 290.5, within 1.1 of 291.6; the company does not state this reconciliation and it is an analyst reading.

## Findings

### Business and transaction view

PENN is a public company without a sponsor or controlling holder disclosed in the supplied text. It runs regional casinos and racetracks and an online sports betting and iCasino business across North America, and its real estate sits mostly with landlords under long-dated triple net leases. For a creditor the structure matters more than the brand: the retail segments produce the cash flow, rent is a fixed and escalating operating cost paid before debt service and a lease default is also a debt default, and the Interactive segment is moving toward break-even by cutting cost rather than by growing underlying revenue. The 2026 transactions were refinancings and development financings rather than a change of control: a new 600.0 unsecured note, extended bank maturities, and sale-leaseback funding from GLPI for the Aurora project. The history that matters is the 2023 Barstool round trip, the 2023 to 2025 ESPN relationship and its early end, the 2025 to 2026 activist contest settled by a cooperation agreement, and the shift from buybacks in 2025 to none in 2026. ### Credit translations

1. Landlord claims and cross-default. Evidence: the AR PENN and 2023 Master Leases are "cross-defaulted, cross-collateralized, and coterminous, and subject to a parent guarantee" (10-Q Q3 page:21), and a default under a master lease "could result in a default under our debt agreements" (10-K page:35). Risk mechanic: a lease default or termination removes operating properties and accelerates debt through cross-default, so lease performance gates the whole capital structure. Credit implication: lease coverage and rent escalation are first-order credit drivers alongside debt leverage; GLPI funding of development raises fixed rent (analyst arithmetic: 10.1, 11.7 and 17.4 of added annual rent on 130.0, 150.0 and 216.3 of funding, or 7.9% on 496.3 in total). 2. Refinancing and maturity. Evidence: bank facilities now mature in 2031 and 2033 and 600.0 of notes was issued due 2031 (10-Q Q3 pages 17-18). Risk mechanic: the near-term maturity wall is the 400.0 of notes due January 15, 2027, treated as long-term on intent and ability to refinance, with liquidity of 2020.9 (CP-1) available. Credit implication: refinancing risk is low in the next twelve months on liquidity but depends on market access for the 2027 and 2029 notes; the term loans are floating (weighted-average rates of 6.600% to 6.941% across maturity buckets, 10-Q Q3 page:78). Category: Analyst Interpretation.

3. Interactive durability. Evidence: Interactive revenue rose 50.7 in Q3 2026 while the tax gross-up rose by 51.9 and online gaming revenue fell, with the loss narrowing on lower marketing, general and administrative, and labor costs (10-Q Q3 page:64). Risk mechanic: the segment's improved result rests on cost removal after the ESPN agreement ended and may not persist if marketing returns to win share, while revenue ex gross-up is flat. Credit implication: a recovery in consolidated earnings is partly dependent on an unproven profit path; the conflict list shows none that counters it. Category: Analyst Interpretation.

4. Sponsor and shareholder alignment. Evidence: no sponsor, no dividends, buybacks of 354.4 in FY2025 and none in nine months 2026, and 750.0 of authorization to 2028 (10-Q Q3 page:80). Risk mechanic: management discretion over cash returns is not constrained in the pages read, and the activist settlement refreshed the board. Credit implication: monitor restricted-payment capacity and repurchase resumption against the 2027 maturity; Not assessable without the debt documents. Category: Analyst Interpretation with Insufficient Information on covenants.

5. Collateral and recovery mechanics (no recovery conclusion). Evidence: interests in owned real property, with named exceptions, collateralize the credit facilities (10-K page:64) while the majority of real estate is leased (10-Q Q3 page:7). Risk mechanic: owned real property available to secure bank debt is limited by the leased structure, and landlord rights rank through lease terms. Credit implication: recovery would depend on lease treatment as well as asset value; value and priority are Not supplied. Category: Analyst Interpretation.

spans.text: ## Request

PENN Entertainment, Inc. as of 2026-11-05, credit_snapshot pathway, USD, covering the fundamental credit synthesis for q3-2026 against fy-2025. The synthesis uses the earlier financial and business handoffs only.
## Sources
### Issuer sources behind the handoffs
This module reads no source text. It lists the seven pinned sources because every figure and fact it uses was drawn from them by the earlier modules.
| Source name | sha256 |
### Supplied handoffs
| Module | sha256 |
| CP-0 | 8e6b52c72fe186ee073cb0e5f0c242ec3f53d4e3a091c87a50ef71a77d1acea5 |

Consistency with the handoffs: this synthesis corrects none of them. CP-1A rated its readiness for CP-2 as ready with limits, which is a signal that caps confidence below High. Basis is cited in brackets as the handoff and section, for example [CP-1 Chart data: leverage] or [CP-1A Company and operating model].
## Findings
### Reader summary
| Bottom line | Confidence | Main limitation |

| PENN's credit profile is improving, with strong near-term liquidity and a longer bank maturity profile, but large landlord obligations outside debt and a still loss-making online segment keep the view cautious. | Medium | Credit agreement, indentures, lease texts and ratings are not supplied, so covenant headroom and creditor protections cannot be tested. |
| Finding | Creditor impact | Confidence |

| Net debt over LTM Consolidated Adjusted EBITDA fell to 1.62x from 2.67x, and liquidity is USD 2,020.9 million. | Near-term refinancing and debt service are well covered on the company's debt measure. | Medium |

| Lease and financing obligations of USD 8,157.6 million sit outside debt; adding financing obligations and finance leases lifts net leverage to 5.63x. | Fixed landlord claims, which cross-default into debt, are the main structural burden. | Medium |

| The online segment's loss narrowed to USD 18.3 million in Q3 2026, but revenue excluding tax pass-through was flat to lower. | Earnings improvement rests on cost reduction that may not persist. | Medium |
| Cash interest cover is 2.85x on LTM Consolidated Adjusted EBITDA, up from 2.17x for FY2025. | Cover is improving but leaves limited cushion against fixed charges. | Medium |
### Credit view

PENN's fundamental credit profile is improving but still burdened by landlord obligations, so the view is constructive on liquidity and refinancing and cautious on fixed charges. The strongest support is liquidity of USD 2,020.9 million and net debt of 1.62x LTM Consolidated Adjusted EBITDA of USD 1,088.2 million, with bank maturities pushed to 2031 and 2033. The weakest point is that USD 8,157.6 million of lease and financing obligations sit outside debt and cross-default into the debt agreements, and that the online segment still loses money. What decides the outcome is whether the retail margin gains and online cost savings hold while rent escalates, and whether the USD 400.0 million of notes due January 15, 2027 are refinanced on acceptable terms. [CP-1; CP-1A]
### Key findings

PENN's reported leverage fell through 2026 on the company's own definition. Total debt over LTM Consolidated Adjusted EBITDA is 2.58x against 3.50x at FY2025, and net debt over EBITDA is 1.62x against 2.67x, as cash rose to USD 1,044.8 million and EBITDA rose to USD 1,088.2 million from USD 830.1 million [CP-1 Chart data: leverage]. The measure is management's non-GAAP view struck after triple net operating lease rent and it leaves out USD 4,359.4 million of financing obligations and finance leases, so an extended perimeter that adds them gives net leverage of 5.63x [CP-1 Calculations]. Creditors should therefore treat the improvement as real but read the level against the landlord claims, not against the headline ratio.

Liquidity is the clearest strength. Cash of USD 1,044.8 million plus an undrawn revolver of USD 976.1 million gives USD 2,020.9 million, against USD 432.3 million of debt maturing in the next twelve months and no committed facility located that expires within that period [CP-1 Chart data: liquidity; CP-1 Calculations]. The 2026 refinancing extended the revolver and Term Loan A to April 2031 and Term Loan B to May 2033 and added USD 600.0 million of 6.75% notes due 2031 [CP-1A Transaction summary and new debt issues]. The near-term maturity that remains is the USD 400.0 million of 5.625% notes due January 15, 2027, which the company classifies as long-term on its intent and ability to refinance.

The earnings recovery has two unequal sources. Retail Segment Adjusted EBITDAR was USD 501.8 million in Q3 2026 against USD 465.8 million, with the margin at 33.7% against 32.8% [CP-1 Financials and credit metrics]. The online segment's loss narrowed to USD 18.3 million from USD 76.6 million, but revenue excluding the gaming tax gross-up was USD 157.0 million against USD 158.2 million, and online gaming revenue fell, so the gain came from lower marketing, general and administrative and labor costs after the ESPN agreement ended [CP-1; CP-1A Company and operating model]. That makes part of the earnings recovery depend on keeping costs low.

Fixed charges remain heavy. LTM cash paid for interest of USD 382.4 million gives cash interest cover of 2.85x on LTM Consolidated Adjusted EBITDA, up from 2.17x at FY2025 [CP-1 Chart data: interest cover]. Leases are the structural issue: the AR PENN and 2023 Master Leases are cross-defaulted and a master lease default could trigger a default under the debt agreements, and the development funding GLPI provides adds annual rent of about 7.9% of the funds received [CP-1A Credit translations]. Covenant headroom is not measurable: the maximum total net leverage of 4.50x and minimum interest coverage of 2.00x are printed but the reported ratios and definitions are not supplied [CP-1 Covenants].
### Strengths and weaknesses

Strengths. Liquidity and refinancing runway [Documentary Fact]: PENN holds cash of USD 1,044.8 million and an undrawn revolver of USD 976.1 million maturing April 2031, so liquidity of USD 2,020.9 million covers the USD 432.3 million of twelve-month maturities several times over, and bank maturities now sit in 2031 and 2033 [CP-1 Chart data: liquidity; CP-1A Transaction summary and new debt issues]. Deleveraging on management measures [Documentary Fact for the figures, Analyst Interpretation for the reading]: total debt fell to USD 2,806.6 million from USD 2,904.1 million while LTM Consolidated Adjusted EBITDA rose to USD 1,088.2 million, giving 2.58x gross and 1.62x net, which lowers the burden of the floating term loans and eases refinancing [CP-1 Chart data: leverage]. Retail earnings power [Documentary Fact]: Segment Adjusted EBITDAR of USD 501.8 million in Q3 2026 on a 33.7% margin, spread across 28 jurisdictions and 42 gaming and racing properties, supports cash flow from a diversified base [CP-1 Financials and credit metrics; CP-1A Company and operating model]. Governance record [Analyst Interpretation]: no priming, uptier, drop-down or collateral release was found, buybacks of USD 354.4 million in FY2025 stopped in nine months 2026, and the February 2026 activist settlement removed an open contest, which is supportive of creditors though the debt documents that would constrain future behaviour are not supplied [CP-1A Ownership, governance and capital allocation].

Weaknesses. Landlord obligations [Documentary Fact for amounts, Analyst Interpretation for the reading]: lease and financing obligations of USD 8,157.6 million sit outside the debt figure, of which USD 4,359.4 million is not deducted in EBITDA, so fixed-charge leverage is far higher than the headline, and a lease default is also a debt default [CP-1 Claims outside debt; CP-1A Credit translations]. Online segment [Analyst Interpretation]: a loss of USD 18.3 million in Q3 2026 and a loss of USD 78.6 million over the LTM period mean the segment still consumes cash, and the improvement rests on cost cuts with revenue ex gross-up flat, so earnings could slip if marketing returns [CP-1A Company and operating model]. Interest burden [Documentary Fact]: cash interest of USD 382.4 million against LTM Consolidated Adjusted EBITDA of USD 1,088.2 million leaves cover of 2.85x, and LTM net income was a loss of USD 11.0 million [CP-1 Financials and credit metrics]. Earnings quality [Documentary Fact]: Consolidated Adjusted EBITDA is a management measure that adds back items including USD 44.9 million labelled Other for nine months 2026, so its underlying level cannot be tested against the ledger [CP-1 Quality and definition notes on EBITDA]. Information gaps [Insufficient Information]: covenant ratios, guarantor identity, restricted-payment capacity, large-holder data and ratings are not supplied, which prevents a view on headroom and creditor protections and limits confidence to Medium [CP-0; CP-1A Gaps].
### Credit assessment
| Element | Judgment | Category | Confidence | Basis |

| Fundamental credit view | Improving profile; constructive on liquidity and refinancing, cautious on landlord-driven fixed charges and the online segment | Analyst Interpretation | Medium | CP-1 leverage, liquidity, interest cover charts; CP-1A Credit translations |

| Thesis | PENN's stronger liquidity, longer bank maturities and lower management-basis leverage support the credit, but fixed landlord obligations that cross-default into the debt and a still loss-making online segment limit how far the view can improve | Analyst Interpretation | Medium | As above |
| Covenant headroom | Not assessable: ratios and definitions not supplied | Insufficient Information | Not assessable | CP-1 Covenants; CP-0 Gaps |
### Key credit risks
| Risk | Mechanic | Credit implication | Severity |

| Lease cross-default and rent escalation | Master lease default or termination removes properties and can trigger debt default; development funding adds rent at about 7.9% of funds received; rent escalators continue | First-order link between lease performance and debt; lease coverage matters alongside leverage | Material |

| Online segment durability | Improvement came from lower marketing, general and administrative and labor costs; revenue excluding gross-up USD 157.0 million against USD 158.2 million | Earnings recovery may reverse if costs rise or competition requires spend | Material |

| Refinancing of 2027 and 2029 notes | USD 400.0 million due January 15, 2027 and USD 400.0 million in 2029; fair values of the 2029 and 2031 notes are below principal in the filing | Depends on market access; liquidity covers the first maturity | Material |
| Covenant and document opacity | Covenant ratios, definitions and restricted-payment capacity not supplied | Cannot test headroom, distribution capacity or collateral priority | Material |

| Discretionary demand, competition and gaming tax | Slot-driven regional revenue; Northeast gaming tax ratio 40.3%; new supply, substitutes and prediction markets | Cash flow follows consumer spend and state tax policy | Material |
| Shareholder returns resume | USD 750.0 million repurchase authorization remains to 2028 and no dividends are paid | Cash could compete with debt reduction; constraints unknown | Minor |
| Floating-rate exposure | Term loans are floating at weighted-average rates of 6.600% to 6.941% | Higher rates raise cash interest; no hedge located | Minor |
## Calculations

No new calculation is made in this module. Every figure is carried unchanged from CP-1 and CP-1A, including the ratios 2.58x, 1.62x, 5.63x and 2.85x and the amounts USD 2,020.9 million and USD 8,157.6 million. The CP-1 calculations were rechecked from the handoff inputs: 2,806.6 divided by 1,088.2 and 1,761.8 divided by 1,088.2 give the stated gross and net ratios, and 1,088.2 divided by 382.4 gives the stated interest cover.
## Gaps
| Gap | Severity | What it affects | Action |

| Credit agreement, indentures, master lease texts and compliance certificate not supplied | Material | Covenant headroom, restricted payments, guarantors, cross-default and cure mechanics | Obtain the executed documents and the compliance certificate |
| Ratings, quotes and market data not supplied | Minor | No external view of risk to compare with the fundamental view | Supply if the committee needs it |
| Proxy statement and large-holder data not supplied | Minor | Control and alignment cannot be assessed beyond documented actions | Obtain the 2026 proxy |
| Management outlook amounts not supplied | Minor | No forward earnings view; the synthesis is backward-looking | Obtain outlook materials |
| CP-1A readiness for CP-2 is ready with limits, not fully ready | Material | Confidence cannot be High | Carry the limitation; no change in the view |
| Online segment profit path and revenue ex gross-up are the only evidence for durability | Minor | Medium confidence on the recovery | Track the next quarter |
| Status and scope: this synthesis is restricted to the pinned sources through 2026-11-05 and the three handoffs; text extraction only | Minor | Figures and locators are as in the handoffs | None |
## Next module

CP-5 should trace each cited figure in this synthesis back to its CP-1 or CP-1A handoff, check that the extended-perimeter leverage of 5.63x is described as an analyst construction, and confirm that the Medium confidence follows from the missing debt documents. Relative value and security selection are outside this module.

spans.text: ## Request

PENN Entertainment, Inc., as of 2026-11-05, credit_snapshot pathway, USD. This module traces the claims in the readiness, financial, business and synthesis handoffs back to the seven pinned sources, recomputes their arithmetic, checks them against one another, and grades the run. It is independent of the modules it reviews and corrects them in this handoff only; the earlier handoffs cannot be edited.
## Sources
### Issuer sources re-read for the audit
| Source name | sha256 |
Locators are `source page:N` where N is the extraction chunk number. "10-Q Q3" is the 10-Q for the quarter ended 2026-09-30; "release Q3" is the exhibit dated 2026-11-05.
### Supplied handoffs
| Module | sha256 |
| CP-0 | 8e6b52c72fe186ee073cb0e5f0c242ec3f53d4e3a091c87a50ef71a77d1acea5 |

Each handoff was opened and compared with the sources, not only with the other handoffs. Where this handoff differs from an earlier one it says so and gives the corrected statement; the earlier handoff stays as accepted.
## Findings
### Reader summary
| Bottom line | Confidence | Main limitation |

| The headline debt, liquidity, earnings and leverage figures trace to the filings and recompute exactly. Six minor issues were found and are corrected here; none changes a credit conclusion. | Medium | Review used extracted text, not rendered filings, and the debt documents are not supplied, so covenant and legal claims rest on filing summaries. |
| Finding | Creditor impact | Confidence |

| Debt of 2,806.6, cash of 1,044.8, liquidity of 2,020.9 and LTM Consolidated Adjusted EBITDA of 1,088.2 match the sources and tie to their components. | The core leverage and liquidity picture can be relied on within the stated definitions. | High |

| Three cash-flow lines cite the wrong page, and one statement about landlord payments should read 263.3 rather than 252.2. | Neither changes a ratio; the corrected landlord payment figure is the cash not deducted in EBITDA. | High |
| The 4.125% notes are senior unsecured and not subsidiary guaranteed, which an earlier handoff listed as not located. | The 2029 notes rank with the other notes; the gap is closed. | High |
| Covenant headroom, guarantor identity and lease terms rest on filing summaries because the executed documents are not supplied. | Legal protections cannot be verified from this record. | Medium |
### Evidence trace view

Every material claim in the four handoffs was traced to a located source span, and the arithmetic was recomputed from the cited figures. The headline financial claims hold: debt principal of 2,806.6 and cash of 1,044.8 at 2026-09-30, liquidity of 2,020.9, LTM Consolidated Adjusted EBITDA of 1,088.2, and the ratios derived from them, all recompute exactly and share one perimeter and period basis. A set of 186 figure and phrase checks against the cited pages found 179 at the cited location; the other 7 were examined individually and two were real locator errors, the rest check-string artifacts or an adjacent page already cited. The audit found six issues, all minor: wrong page numbers for three cash-flow lines and one working-capital reference, a statement that gaming taxes are the largest retail cost that is true for only two of four retail segments, a landlord-payment figure of 252.2 that should read 263.3, a gap for the 4.125% notes that the 10-K fills, and a cross-default described more broadly than the filing supports in two handoffs. None changes a ratio, a liquidity figure or the direction of the credit view, so the run is graded Passed with corrections logged. The strongest contrary reading is that the improvement is overstated: the company's debt measure leaves out financing obligations and finance leases of 4,359.4 and LTM net income is a loss of 11.0, so the handoffs already carry the extended-perimeter leverage of 5.63x. What would make the contrary view win is covenant definitions that count those obligations as debt, which the missing credit agreement prevents anyone from testing.
### Quality assurance status
| Field | Value |
| qa_status | Passed (six Minor issues, no Critical or Material issue) |
| committee_status | Draft Only: usable for discussion; covenant, guarantor and lease-term conclusions need the executed documents |
| Confidence band | Medium, capped because the debt documents, ratings and proxy data are not supplied and the checks used extracted text |
| Subsequent events | Handled correctly: the October 15, 2026 exchangeable share notice and the November 1, 2026 rent escalator are labelled subsequent and not blended into period figures |
| Cutoff | No source dated after 2026-11-05 was used |
### Input module register
| Module | Status | Material claims audited | Result |
| CP-0 | Accepted | Source coverage, periods, perimeter, 9 tie-outs | Supported; one locator corrected before acceptance |
| CP-1 | Accepted on second attempt | Statements, debt table, liquidity, maturities, leases, covenants, events, 4 charts | Supported with three issues (I1, I4, I5) |
| CP-1A | Accepted | Business model, profile, timeline, governance, 5 credit translations | Supported with three issues (I2, I3, I6) |
| CP-2 | Accepted | Credit view, findings, strengths, weaknesses, 7 risks | Supported; repeats the I6 wording and is otherwise consistent |
### Citation and evidence support audit
| Claim | Module | Locator checked | Result |
| Debt table, repayment schedule and total of 2,806.6 | CP-1 | 10-Q Q3 pages 15-16 | Supported |
| Revolver 1.0 billion, letters of credit 23.9, availability 976.1, maturity April 2031 | CP-1 | 10-Q Q3 pages 17-18 | Supported |
| Covenant levels 4.50 to 1.00, step up 5.00 to 1.00, 2.00 to 1.00, compliance statement | CP-1 | 10-Q Q3 pages 17 and 20 | Supported; ratio values not printed |
| Lease and financing obligation balances 2,309.8, 2,049.6, 3,798.2 | CP-1 | 10-Q Q3 pages 2 and 27 | Supported |

| Cash-flow lines: operating cash flow 626.4 and 401.0, capital expenditures 251.2 and 457.3, sale-leaseback proceeds 216.3 and 130.0 | CP-1 | Cited as 10-Q Q3 page:6; found on page:5 | Figures supported, locator wrong (issue I1) |
| Cash paid for interest 291.6 and 292.2, no share repurchases | CP-1 | 10-Q Q3 page:6 | Supported |
| LTM Consolidated Adjusted EBITDA 1,088.2, 999.1, 922.6 and FY2025 830.1 | CP-1 | Releases, 10-K page:74 | Supported as management measures |
| Segment Adjusted EBITDAR and revenue by segment | CP-1; CP-1A | 10-Q Q3 pages 15, 38, 40 | Supported |

| "Gaming taxes are the largest retail cost" | CP-1A | 10-Q Q3 page:37 | Partly supported (issue I3): true in Northeast (285.8) and Midwest (89.4); in South other segment items (67.3) exceed compensation (58.2) and gaming taxes (58.0); in West compensation (35.4) exceeds other items (34.9) and gaming taxes (26.3) |

| "252.2 is the part of landlord payments not deducted in EBITDA" | CP-1 | 10-Q Q3 pages 27 and 28 | Incorrect attribution (issue I4); see below |

| 4.125% Notes "ranking and guarantor wording not located" | CP-1 | 10-K page:139 | Gap fillable (issue I5): "4.125% senior unsecured notes", due July 1, 2029, issued at par, interest each January 1 and July 1, "not guaranteed by any of the Company's subsidiaries" except if certain guaranteed securities are later issued, redeemable from July 1, 2024 |

| Lease default is also a debt default | CP-1A; CP-2 | 10-Q Q3 page:20; 10-K page:35 | Overbroad (issue I6): the debt agreements cross-default to the Master Leases with GLPI; the 10-K names the AR PENN, 2023 and Pinnacle Master Leases. VICI Master Lease and Morgantown Lease cross-default is not stated |
| Interactive revenue ex gross-up 157.0 against 158.2; nine months 493.3 against 498.3 | CP-1; CP-1A; CP-2 | 10-Q Q3 pages 15, 56, 64 | Supported |
| ESPN-related advertising 52.0 in Q3 2025 | CP-1 | 10-Q Q3 page:41 | Supported |
| GLPI funding 130.0, 150.0, 216.3 and added rent 10.1, 11.7, 17.4 | CP-1A | 10-Q Q3 pages 22-23, 49-50 | Supported |
| Business facts: 28 jurisdictions, 42 properties in 19 states, employees, footprint | CP-1A | 10-K pages 6-7, 9, 21 | Supported (properties are at 2025-12-31) |
| Governance: HG Vora timeline, Cooperation Agreement, buybacks, authorization 750.0 | CP-1A | 10-K pages 29-30, 109; 10-Q Q3 page:80 | Supported |
| Pension, retiree medical and factoring obligations not found | CP-1 | Search of the 10-K and 10-Q Q3 | Supported by search |
| No creditor-adverse action found | CP-1A | Search for priming, uptier, drop-down and similar terms across the filings | Supported by search; the hits were betting "liability management" |
| Guidance amounts not supplied | CP-0; CP-1 | Search of releases and filings | Supported; only a full-year Interactive target is referred to, with no amount |
### Legal and structural claims audit
| Claim | Basis in the handoffs | Result |

| Notes are senior unsecured and not subsidiary guaranteed (5.625%, 4.125%, 6.75%) | Filing descriptions, 10-Q Q3 page:18; 10-K page:139 | Supported by filing text; indentures not supplied, so clause-level support is absent |
| Credit facility obligations are collateralised by interests in owned real property with named exceptions | 10-K page:64 | Supported by filing text; security package and guarantors not supplied |
| AR PENN and 2023 Master Leases are cross-defaulted, cross-collateralized, coterminous and subject to a parent guarantee | 10-Q Q3 page:21 | Supported by filing text; lease documents not supplied |
| Debt agreements cross-default to the GLPI Master Leases | 10-Q Q3 page:20; 10-K page:35 | Supported with the scope noted in issue I6 |
| Covenant tests and levels | 10-Q Q3 page:17 | Supported; definitions and reported values not supplied, headroom correctly stated as Not calculable |
| Lease terms, escalators and rent resets | 10-Q Q3 pages 21-25 | Supported by filing text |
### Relative value and market claims audit
| Claim | Result |
| Fair values of 574.5 for the 6.75% notes and 375.0 for the 4.125% notes below principal (10-Q Q3 page:78) | Supported as disclosed fair values; the handoffs use them as a fact, not a price view |
| No peer ranking, instrument recommendation or recovery conclusion | None found in any handoff; CP-1A recovery mechanics are stated without an outcome |
### Cross-module consistency and version control
| Item | CP-1 | CP-1A | CP-2 | Result |
| Debt principal at 2026-09-30 | 2,806.6 | 2806.6 (cited from CP-1) | 2,806.6 | Consistent |
| Cash at 2026-09-30 | 1,044.8 | Not restated | 1,044.8 | Consistent |
| Liquidity | 2,020.9 | Not restated | 2,020.9 | Consistent |
| LTM Consolidated Adjusted EBITDA | 1,088.2 | 1088.2 (cited from CP-1) | 1,088.2 | Consistent |
| Net and gross leverage | 1.62x and 2.58x | Not restated | 1.62x and 2.58x | Consistent |
| Obligations outside debt | 8,157.6 | 8157.6 | 8,157.6 | Consistent |
| Extended-perimeter net leverage | 5.63x | Not restated | 5.63x | Consistent, labelled analyst construction |
| Retail margin Q3 2026 | 33.7% | 33.7% | 33.7% | Consistent |
| Added rent on GLPI funding | Not restated | 7.9% | 7.9% | Consistent |
| Cross-default scope | Tied to the Master Leases (accurate) | General | General | CP-1A and CP-2 are broader than the filings (issue I6) |

Version control: the debt table changed version in 2026 (revolver and Term Loan A to 2031, Term Loan B to 2033). CP-1 labels the year-end 2025 table as the prior version; no handoff mixes the two without a label. The 2029 notes are the same instrument at both dates.
### Duplication, materiality and committee readiness

CP-2 repeats figures from CP-1 and CP-1A by design and adds no figure of its own. The reader summaries restate conclusions already in each handoff. The covenant limitation is repeated in every module; it is material because it blocks the headroom conclusion, so the repetition is acceptable. No duplicated analysis changes a conclusion. The run is usable as a filings-based snapshot for discussion.
### Handoff envelope and evidence trace audit
| Module | Six H2 headings in order | Issuer and as-of date in Request | Sources and hashes listed | Handoffs listed with hashes | Selector headings present once | Result |
| CP-0 | Yes | Yes | Yes | None supplied (correct) | Reader summary and Readiness view | Pass |
| CP-1 | Yes | Yes | Yes | CP-0 | Four chart tables, financials table | Pass |
| CP-1A | Yes | Yes | Yes | CP-0, CP-1 | Operating model, profile, transaction summary | Pass |
| CP-2 | Yes | Yes | Yes | CP-0, CP-1, CP-1A | Key findings, strengths and weaknesses | Pass |
### Consolidated issue log
| Issue | Severity | Module | Type | Description and correction | Status |
| I1 | Minor | CP-1 | Locator | Operating cash flow, capital expenditures and sale-leaseback proceeds are cited to 10-Q Q3 page:6; they are on page:5. Figures are correct. | Corrected here |
| I2 | Minor | CP-1A | Locator | Working capital row cites 10-Q Q3 page:6; the accrued expense and prepaid lines are on page:5. | Corrected here |

| I3 | Minor | CP-1A | Unsupported superlative | Gaming taxes are the largest retail cost line only in Northeast and Midwest. In South the largest line in Q3 2026 is other segment items (67.3, against compensation 58.2 and gaming taxes 58.0); in West it is compensation (35.4, against other segment items 34.9 and gaming taxes 26.3). | Corrected here |

| I4 | Minor | CP-1 | Attribution | CP-1 says the excess of landlord cash payments (746.6) over operating lease rent expense (494.4) of 252.2 is the part not deducted in EBITDA. The cash not deducted is the Pinnacle Master Lease and Morgantown Lease payments of 260.9 and 2.4, which is 263.3 (10-Q Q3 page:27). The 252.2 also reflects operating lease rent expense of 494.4 exceeding the 483.3 paid under the AR PENN, 2023 and VICI leases (219.3, 203.2, 60.8) by 11.1. | Corrected here |

| I5 | Minor | CP-1 | Fillable gap | The 4.125% Notes are described in the 10-K at page:139 as senior unsecured, due July 1, 2029, not guaranteed by subsidiaries; the Q3 10-Q does not repeat it. | Corrected here |

| I6 | Minor | CP-1A; CP-2 | Overbreadth | Cross-default to leases is stated for GLPI Master Leases in the filings, not for all landlord leases. The credit conclusion stands because the GLPI leases carry most of the rent. | Corrected here |
### Remediation priority map

Must fix before committee: none. Must fix before the handoffs are consumed downstream: read I1 to I6 with the accepted handoffs, in particular use 263.3 as the landlord cash not deducted in EBITDA, and use the GLPI Master Leases scope for cross-default. Monitoring follow-up: obtain the credit agreement, compliance certificate, indentures and executed leases, and re-run the covenant and cross-default conclusions. Formatting and hygiene: use `page:5` for the cash-flow lines and carry the corrected 4.125% notes description.
### Clearance decision

CLEARANCE DECISION: Pass with corrections. Critical issues: 0. Material issues: 0. Minor issues: 6. The run may be used as a filings-based snapshot for committee discussion (status Draft Only) with the corrections above and the limits on covenant, guarantor and lease-term conclusions. It does not clear any conclusion that needs the executed debt or lease documents.
## Calculations
All inputs come from the cited locators; amounts in US$m. Each handoff value was recomputed.
| Metric | Inputs | Recomputed | Handoff | Result |
| Extended-perimeter leverage | (2,806.6 + 4,359.4) / 1,088.2; less cash 1,044.8 | 6.585; 5.625 | 6.59x; 5.63x | Match |
| Twelve-month maturity cover | 2,020.9 / 432.3, with 432.3 = 400.0 + 32.3 | 4.675 | 4.7 times | Match |
| LTM operating cash flow, capital expenditures | 508.2 + 626.4 - 401.0; 647.7 + 251.2 - 457.3 | 733.6; 441.6 | 733.6; 441.6 | Match |
| Landlord cash not deducted in EBITDA, nine months 2026 | 260.9 + 2.4 (Pinnacle and Morgantown); check 746.6 - (219.3 + 203.2 + 60.8) | 263.3; 263.3 | CP-1 stated 252.2 | Corrected (issue I4) |
| Rent expense LTM | 631.7 + 494.4 - 470.0 | 656.1 | 656.2 printed | 0.1 rounding in the source, disclosed in CP-1 |

Consistency of period and perimeter: every LTM figure combines the audited year, the nine months 2026 and the nine months 2025 on the consolidated perimeter; the debt figures are principal while the balance sheet carrying value is 2,768.3, a difference of 38.3 of discounts and costs that CP-1 states.
## Gaps
| Gap | Effect on the audit | Action |

| Executed credit agreement, indentures, master leases and compliance certificate not supplied | Legal and covenant claims rest on filing summaries, so clause-level support is absent | Obtain and re-audit |

| Review used extracted text with chunk numbers, not rendered filings or XBRL | A flattened table could hide a sign or column error; the recomputations reduce this risk | Spot check the figures that drive conclusions |
| Ratings, quotes, proxy ownership data and guidance amounts not supplied | Not audited | Supply if needed |
| Guarantor identity for the credit facilities not located | Priority of bank debt against notes not testable | Obtain guarantor schedule |
| Confidence is capped at Medium | Reflects the gaps above, not a defect in the handoffs | None |
## Next module

This is the last module in the run. The report should assemble the four handoffs together with the six corrections in the issue log: page:5 for the cash-flow lines, the corrected gaming tax statement, 263.3 as the landlord cash not deducted in EBITDA, the 4.125% notes description, and the GLPI scope of cross-default. Any later work should start from the debt and lease documents.
